_what: Every narration sentence maps to a span of script/essay.txt, the assembled sources of record for this film.
thesis: Three valuations of one ordinary object disagree; Chang took the disagreement as the material, destroyed the coins into a block and inscribed them, and the value of what remains goes on being redefined after the coin itself has stopped being made.
script_target: About 3 minutes. 24 lines, 357 words, 28 sentences; 188-165s of speech at 114-130 wpm, plus 4s for credits.

claims.say: For more than a century the penny has circulated, considered a worthless nuisance.
claims.span: so commonplace that it is considered a worthless nuisance
claims.epoch_note: Source states it in the present. Still true in 2026: production ended November 2025 but the coins remain legal tender and circulate, so the present perfect is accurate rather than inherited.

claims.say: To the Treasury it is worth exactly one cent, whatever year it was struck, and always will be.
claims.span: a penny from any given year will always be worth exactly 1¢, according to the United States Treasury
claims.epoch_note: The span says 'will always be worth exactly 1 cent', so 'always will be' is supported and not an extrapolation.

claims.say: Those struck before 1983 are copper, and in March 2024 that copper was worth about three cents.
claims.span: those minted in 1982 and before were struck in copper and now have a metal value of approximately 3.1¢
claims.note: EPOCH: 'in 2024' is stated because this is a moving figure. The source is the project description, dated 2024-03-26 and contemporaneous with the work. The Medium essay's later 2.5¢ is noted in block [8] and not used.
claims.epoch_note: THE MODEL CASE. The span reads 'now have a metal value of approximately 3.1 cents'. That 'now' is March 2024 and is converted to an absolute date in narration.

claims.say: Three valuations of one small object, and no two of them agree.
claims.span: Recognizing these discrepancies in value
claims.note: The three valuations are lines 1-3: treated as worthless, fixed at 1¢ by the Treasury, about 3¢ as copper. The source's word is 'discrepancies', plural.
claims.epoch: standing claim; the copper figure it rests on is epoched at line 3
claims.epoch_note: The structural claim (the valuations disagree) does not expire; only the figure does, and the figure carries its own date one line earlier.

claims.say: Recognising those discrepancies, Rutherford Chang removed ten thousand copper cents from circulation and called the work CENTS.
claims.span: Recognizing these discrepancies in value, Rutherford Chang removed 10,000 copper cents from circulation and archivally documented them
claims.epoch_note: The period of collecting and removal, per the work's own dates CENTS #1-10,000, 2017-2024.

claims.say: He had spent his working life collecting ordinary things until time made them singular.
claims.span: An artist of accumulation, repetition and the slow revaluation of ordinary things

claims.say: More than three and a half thousand copies of the same Beatles record, no two worn alike.
claims.span: The materials list for the UCCA retrospective (2026) gives 3,555 records and a neon sign
claims.note: CURRENT FIGURE. The NYT obituary (Feb 2025) gives more than 3,400; the collection grew until he died, so 3,555 supersedes it. 'More than three and a half thousand' is true of 3,555 and not of the superseded count.
claims.epoch: 2006-2025 for the collection; the count is the 2026 figure
claims.epoch_note: Two figures exist: the NYT obituary (Feb 2025) gives more than 3,400, the UCCA materials list (2026) gives 3,555. 'More than three and a half thousand' uses the later and current figure deliberately.

claims.say: Shown for two decades — the New Museum in New York, the Akademie der Künste in Berlin, Kunsthal Rotterdam.
claims.span: NOTHINGTOSEENESS, Akademie der Kuenste, Berlin, 2021; Kunsthal Rotterdam, 2020; Deichtorhallen, Hamburg, 2019; Rhizome and the New Museum, New York, 2016
claims.note: Two anchors spanning the record rather than a list. 'Two decades' is the 2002-2024 span of the artist's own exhibition list.
claims.epoch_note: Replaced ICA London 2005 and the Art Gallery of Ontario group show with three heavier institutions from the same record. The UCCA retrospective is deliberately NOT here: it ran Jan-Apr 2026, after his death in February 2025, so naming it before line 9 would invert the chronology.

claims.say: He died in February 2025, at forty-five, on the day the President ordered the Treasury to stop making pennies.
claims.span: He died in February 2025, at the age of 45
claims.note: The same-day coincidence is block [6]: the order was given on the ninth of February 2025, and the obituary ran that day. Stated in the past tense per the corpus house guidance, with no speculation.
claims.as_of: NYT obituary 9 Feb 2025; penny facts of record
claims.epoch_note: Both events are same-day: the order was announced the evening of 9 February 2025.

claims.say: Every one of the ten thousand was photographed first.
claims.span: Chang photographed each coin to record its particular wear and patina
claims.epoch_note: DETECTOR FALSE POSITIVE: 'first' here is sequential - photographed before being destroyed - not a superlative. Dated anyway because the act has a period.

claims.say: The portrait on them, Victor David Brenner's Lincoln, is the most reproduced artwork on Earth.
claims.span: the portrait of Abraham Lincoln on the cent's obverse is the most reproduced piece of art on Earth
claims.note: Brenner is named from the Medium essay; the project description does not name him. He appears here as a property of the object, after the origin has been given — not as a reason for choosing it.
claims.epoch: standing claim in the source; not independently verified
claims.epoch_note: A superlative about a set nobody can count. Faithful to the source of record, which is the project's own text. Flagged for the author's decision, not resolved here.

claims.say: Two hundred and eighty-eight billion of them in existence, by the project's count in 2024.
claims.span: With approximately 288 billion Lincoln pennies in existence
claims.note: POPULATION NAMED. 'Still in existence' is said aloud because 288 billion surviving and 500+ billion struck are different quantities.
claims.epoch_note: WAS WRONG. The script read 'still in existence'. The source says 'in existence' and is dated March 2024; 'still' is a deictic the narration ADDED, asserting a 2026 measurement nobody made. Now attributed and dated.

claims.say: Circulation made the marks: verdigris, abrasion, a fingerprint, the way each one left.
claims.span: Patina: verdigris, obsidian, desert, red, gold, orange, corroded, iridescent. Wear: abraded, faceless, lustrous, striated. Motif: assassin, fingerprint, ghost, wheat
claims.note: The three named are drawn from the catalogued trait list. 'Circulation made the marks' is the project description's 'The course of history has endowed each of these metal discs with unique characteristics'.

claims.say: No algorithm assigned any of it.
claims.span: Unlike generative 10K collections with algorithmically assigned traits, CENTS traits are derived from real-world physicality
claims.epoch_note: The cataloguing period - two years of community voting. Matched on its span, not its wording.

claims.say: The names came afterwards, from the collectors, over two years of voting.
claims.span: a community-led initiative carried out over the course of 2 years through multiple reviews of the full 10k set, numerous voting rounds
claims.note: The source writes '2 years'; the line says 'two years'. The marks were made by circulation and the NAMES by the Trait Council — the distinction the glossary holds apart.

claims.say: More than half the set carries no mark at all, which is what makes the rest mean anything.
claims.span: 5,306 cents — 53.06 per cent — carry no catalogued visual trait at all
claims.epoch_note: NOW. 5,306 of 10,000 - 53.06 per cent - carry no catalogued trait. A present-moment measurement of a closed set, so it does not expire.

claims.say: Then he destroyed them, smelted into one block of thirty-one kilograms.
claims.span: the physical coins are smelted and cast into a solid 68.56-pound copper block
claims.note: Said as thirty-one kilograms, which is the UCCA figure for the same block; 68.56 lb = 31.1 kg.
claims.epoch_note: 31 kg from the project description's 68.56 pounds.

claims.say: Each photograph he inscribed on a satoshi, the smallest unit of Bitcoin.
claims.span: Images of these 10,000 individuals are inscribed as ordinals on 10,000 satoshis, the smallest units of Bitcoin
claims.epoch_note: The inscriptions were made in 2024; 'smallest unit of Bitcoin' is definitional.

claims.say: The block he had scanned, and inscribed as the whole of Bitcoin block 839969.
claims.span: This metal block is rendered as a three-dimensional digital model and in turn inscribed as a 4-megabyte ordinal, comprising the entirety of Bitcoin block #839969

claims.say: An ingot so dense it cannot be destroyed.
claims.span: Equivalent to casting a copper ingot so heavy and dense that it is indestructible

claims.say: He released all ten thousand at one sat each.
claims.span: he released the 10,000 cent inscriptions for the price of one sat each
claims.epoch_note: The release price. What happened since is a separate claim with its own epoch.

claims.say: By October 2026 the ones listed for sale were asking around three hundred and sixty thousand sats.
claims.span: the listed asking prices observed in October 2026 are around three hundred and sixty thousand satoshis each
claims.epoch_note: NOW. Observed in the CENTS Lab Market interface, asset a13.png, verified 2026-10-06. Says 'listed' and not 'sold': these are asking prices on 198 open listings, not recorded sales and not a valuation of the whole set. This is the only hard present-moment evidence for the film's thesis that the value goes on being redefined.

claims.say: The set is closed.
claims.span: this digitally scarce set of 10,000

claims.say: It stops at 1982, because in 1983 the penny stopped being copper.
claims.span: Cents minted in 1982 and earlier were struck in copper; from 1983 the cent was made of zinc
claims.note: 867 cents are dated 1982 and none later, so the ceiling IS the metallurgical cutoff.
claims.as_of: penny facts of record; catalogue measured 2026-10-08
claims.epoch_note: Historical and fixed.

claims.say: Only one of the years it misses means anything.
claims.span: Only the absence of 1943 is anomalous
claims.note: A claim about a set: fifteen years are absent and only one absence is anomalous. Counted before it was said.
claims.epoch_note: THE COUNTED CLAIM. Fifteen years are absent; only 1943's absence is anomalous, P(zero by chance) 2.75e-05. A claim about a set, established by counting the set, not by one member.

claims.say: In 1943 the copper went to the war, and the cent was struck in steel.
claims.span: In 1943 the United States struck the cent in zinc-coated steel to save copper for the war
claims.epoch_note: Historical and fixed.

claims.say: A set with edges nobody chose.
claims.span: Fifteen years between 1910 and 1982 are absent from the collection
claims.note: Summation of 23-25: a ceiling set by metallurgy and a hole cut by a war, neither curated.
claims.epoch_note: Follows from the material change, not from a choice.

claims.say: The project had described this as coming: the last penny was struck in November 2025.
claims.span: As the traditional penny fades into irrelevance and its production is ultimately terminated
claims.note: The project description is dated 2024-03-26 — a year before the order. 'Which the project had described as coming' refers to that sentence, not to a prediction by the artist.
claims.epoch_note: Past perfect 'had described this as coming' is correct: the project text predates the event.

claims.say: Its value can continue to be redefined through this digitally scarce set of ten thousand, and the block that encapsulates their transformation.
claims.span: its value can continue to be redefined through this digitally scarce set of 10,000 and the block that encapsulates their transformation
claims.note: The work's own closing sentence, quoted. '10,000' is spoken as 'ten thousand'. The source's bridge clause ('as the traditional penny fades into irrelevance') is dropped because keeping it put the line below the quotation threshold — measured, not guessed — so line 27 was reordered to end on the penny, which is what gives 'Its value' its referent.

distinctions_kept.distinction: a PROPERTY of the readymade (the Lincoln portrait's ubiquity) vs the artist's MOTIVE
distinctions_kept.where: the origin is stated in lines 1-5 as three disagreeing valuations; Brenner appears at line 11, after it
distinctions_kept.note: Caught twice by the user. The first film opened on Brenner; so did the first draft of this one. The source itself puts the ubiquity in its second paragraph, after the discrepancies.

distinctions_kept.distinction: the MARKS on a cent (made by circulation) vs the NAMES of its traits (given by the Trait Council)
distinctions_kept.where: lines 13-15 say circulation made the marks and the names came afterwards, from the collectors, over two years of voting

distinctions_kept.distinction: 288 billion IN EXISTENCE vs 500+ billion STRUCK
the end of the PENNY vs the end of CENTS
distinctions_kept.where: line 27 ends the coin; line 28 continues the work. The film's last movement is in the present continuous.

distinctions_kept.distinction: CENTS Block Copper (the physical block) vs CENTS Block 839969 (the inscription of its model)
distinctions_kept.where: line 17 smelts the physical block; line 19 inscribes the scan of it

distinctions_kept.distinction: a melt value NOW vs a melt value WHEN THE WORK WAS MADE
distinctions_kept.where: line 3 says 'in 2024', the epoch of the project description and of the work's completion

epoch_convention: The film speaks from its own present (2026). A source deictic - now, currently, still, today - resolves to the SOURCE'S date and must be converted to an absolute date on the way into narration. Three moments kept distinct: THEN 2017-2024 (March 2024 project description governs), SINCE Feb-Nov 2025, NOW 2026.
